records.name: Preston Capes motte and bailey castle
records.details:
The earthwork remains of the motte and bailey castle at Preston Capes stand on the summit of a north facing spur on the north east side of the village. The motte consists of a conical mound over 4m high with a flat top about 27m across. The motte is surrounded on all sides except the south by a partially waterlogged ditch over 1m deep, and the land slopes steeply in a series of narrow scarps from the edge of the motte ditch. Below the motte on the north- east side, a bank up to 2m high indicates the extent of the original bailey area on that side. The part of the bailey which lay on the flatter ground to the east and south-east of the motte has been built over and archaeological remains are not thought to survive. The motte was the site of a castle built soon after the Norman Conquest, most likely by Nigel of the Count of Mortain who held Preston in 1086. The castle was certainly established by 1090 when it was recorded that Hugh de Leicester founded a Cluniac Priory adjoining his castle at Preston Capes. The site remained as the centre of the manor through the medieval period.

records.name: THE ORCHARD
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES OLD FORGE LANE SP5754 (South side) 15/116 The Orchard - II Cottage. Early C18. Coursed ironstone rubble, thatch roof, brick ridge stacks, one on stone base. 3-unit through-passage plan. 1 storey and attic; 5-window range. Front to garden has plank door to right in C20 gabled porch. Irregular fenestration of 1, 2 and 3-light casement windows. 2 eyebrow dormers with 2-light windows. All with timber lintels. Bay to left an addition (straight joint). C20 1-window addition to right of door. One 3-light stone mullion window to rear and blocked door. Quoins. Interior: open fireplace and stop-chamfered spine beams.

Listing NGR: SP5749854689

records.name: FALCON COTTAGE
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES OLD FORGE LANE SP5754 (South side) 15/118 Falcon Cottage - II Cottage. C18. Coursed ironstone rubble, thatch roof, brick end stacks, that to left on stone base. 2-unit plan. Single storey and attic; 2-window range. Two 2-light casements to ground floor, with timber lintels, a small overlight window in eyebrow dormer to attic. 1-storey extension to right, door to rear. Interior has open fireplace and stop-chamfered spine beams.

Listing NGR: SP5737354722

records.name: HILLCREST
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES HIGH STREET SP5754 (East side) 15/112 Hillcrest GV II Cottage. One of an irregular row of 4 cottages. Early C18. Cruck-framed. Coursed ironstone rubble, tile roof, brick ridge stack on stone base. 2-storey, 2-window range. Plank door to left with stop-chamfered timber lintel and small square leaded overlight with long timber lintel. Similar small square window to left of door, a 2-light casement window above and to right of door, both with timber lintels. Interior: stop-chamfered spine beam and raised cruck truss.

Listing NGR: SP5762554656

records.name: THE WILDERNESS
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES OLD FORGE LANE SP5754 (North side) 15/114 The Wilderness - II House. C18. Coursed squared ironstone, slate roof, C20 brick end stacks. 2-unit plan. 2 storeys; 3-window range. C20 central door with overlight and timber lintel, 2-light casement window above, 3-light casement window to ground and first floors left and right. All windows have timber lintels; those to first floor are stop-chamfered. Interior not inspected.

Listing NGR: SP5752654776

records.name: OLD RECTORY
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/107 Old Rectory GV II House, formerly rectory. Early C18 with earlier origins and large C19 additions. Coursed ironstone rubble, red brick, hipped slate roofs, various brick lateral, ridge and end stacks. 2 storeys and attic. Stone-built core has two 3-light leaded casement windows with timber lintels to ground and first floors to front facing village and a small roof dormer. A part-glazed plank door to right side. Another stone range projects right towards rear of right side with a glazed door immediately to right but largely hidden by slightly lower early C19 brick front range with 3-light leaded casement windows with pointed arch heads and hood moulds, to ground and first floors. Right end of 2nd stone wing facing garden has a 4-light painted stone arch-mullion window to ground floor, an early C19 brick porch with panelled door and fanlight to right and similar 3-light window to first floor. Behind this wing and facing garden a large early C19 brick range of 3 windows with 15-pane sashes and segmental heads. Other sash windows of 12-panes, leaded wood mullion and transom windows and casement windows to rear and side facing churchyard. Interior not inspected.

Listing NGR: SP5745054889

records.name: BRAMLEY COTTAGE CRENDON HIGH LATCHES
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES HIGH STREET SP5754 (East side) 15/110 Bramley Cottage, High Latches and Crendon GV II Row of 3 cottages. C18. Coursed squared ironstone, tile roof, brick ridge and end stacks, some on stone bases. 2-storey; 8-window range. High Latches and Crendon have plank doors, that to former with tiled hood, the latter with C20 gabled porch. 2 and 3-light casement windows to ground floor, 2-light casement to first floor, all with timber lintels. Bramley Cottage has door to left side. High Latches has open fireplace and stop-chamfered spine beams.

Listing NGR: SP5759454764

records.name: DANECOT
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/105 Danecot GV II Cottage. Early C18, altered early C19. Coursed dressed ironstone, pantile roof, brick end stack to right. 1-unit plan. 2 storeys; 2-window range. Central plank door with stop-chamfered wood lintel, 2-light leaded casement windows with pointed arch Gothick heads. Single-storey extension to right with lean-to tin roof and pointed and plank door flanked by blocked pointed arch windows. Similar small blocked window to gable above. Interior has stop-chamfered spine beams. Formerly a Fawsley estate cottage and one of several remodelled in picturesque manner early C19. Included for group value.

Listing NGR: SP5745754824

records.name: CHURCH OF ST PETER AND ST PAUL
records.officialName: Church of St Peter and St Paul
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/102 Church of St. Peter and St. 18/01/68 Paul GV II* Church. C13-C15, restored 1853. Coursed squared ironstone, lead roofs, chancel tiled. Chancel, nave, north and south aisles, west tower. 3-light Perpendicular east window. North side of chancel wall much rebuilt with single low-side lancet window to west and signs of other blocked windows. To south a 3-light mullion window and priest's door to left. Nave has 2 bay clerestory with 2-light mullion windows with C18 leading, plain coped parapet and 2 C18 lead rainwater heads and pipes north and south. North aisle has 3-light Decorated east window with reticulated tracery and hood-mould with label stops, two 2-light Decorated windows either side of north door. North-west and west windows have 2 lights and depressed arch heads. South aisle has 3-light Decorated east window with cusped heads and intersecting tracery, a 3-light arch mullion window with hood-mould, to right of south porch, a 2-light Decorated window to left. South porch has double-chamfered door and holy water stoup. South door within has 4-centred arch head and hood-mould. West and south-west windows of south aisles have similar windows to those in corresponding positions in north aisle. Both aisles extend across sides of west tower. 3 stage west tower with pointed arch and 3-light Perpendicular window above. Belfry stage has 2-light Perpendicular windows. Angle buttresses and battlements. Interior: C17 communion table. East window flanked by Commandment, Creed and Lords prayer boards grouped in pairs vertically and topped by segmental pediments with gilded urns. Chancel roof of 1853. Chancel arch with 3 chamfered mouldings, innermost on polygonal responds. Nave has 3 bay arcades. Westernmost arches cut off by tower. North arcade has octagonal piers, double-chamfered arches, moulded capitals and respond at east end. South arcade has round piers, octagonal abaci and chamfered arches. Nave roof C19, old lean-to roofs to aisles, that of south aisle with stop-chamfered ties. Octagonal Perpendicular font with blank tracery patterns to sides, but built into south-east pier of tower. Some C15 pews. C18 wall monument in chancel. Painted Carolean Royal Arms in west end of south aisle. (Buildings of England: Northants, p.378; Kellys Directory for Northants, 1903).

Listing NGR: SP5742554900

records.name: MANOR FARMHOUSE
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/106 Manor Farmhouse 18/01/68 Formerly listed as Manor Farmhouse including outbuildings) - II Manor house, now farmhouse. C17 with earlier origins, remodelled early C18. Coursed squared ironstone, old tile roofs with brick end and lateral stacks. 2 storeys and attic; 4-window range widely spaced. 6-panel part-glazed door to right of centre with straight hood. Wood mullion and transom window to right with stone sill and lintel with keyblock. One-storey hipped projection to left with one mullion and transom window to front, another to far left. Similar window to first floor. Stone coped gable to left, hipped roof to right. 3 hipped roof dormers. Back has 3-and 4-light stone mullion windows, a lateral stack supported on corbels and a C17 canted stone oriel window on polygonal corbels. Interior: sitting room has moulded cross-beam roof. Stop-chamfered spine beams.

Listing NGR: SP5766254889

records.name: OLD RECTORY, BARN AND COACH HOUSE APPROXIMATELY 10 METRES EAST
records.officialName: Old Rectory, Barn and Coach House Approximately 10 Metres East
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/108 Old Rectory, barn and coach house approx. 10m. E GV II Barn. C18, with early C19 openings inserted for use as stables and coach house. Coursed squared ironstone, slate roof. 2 storeys. Two central stable doors, that to right with 2-light leaded overlight. Stable doors are flanked by large double-leaf coach house doors. Other 1-and 2-light openings have timber lintels. Stone eaves. Stone coped gables with kneelers, right gable with wrought-iron weathervane. Lower 2-storey, 1-window lean-to extension to right. C20 garage doors behind to right gable end. Some stalls preserved inside. Included for group value.

Listing NGR: SP5748054881

records.name: VILLAGE FARMHOUSE
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES HIGH STREET SP5754 (East side) 15/111 Village Farmhouse GV II Farmhouse. C18. Coursed ironstone rubble, slate roof, brick ridge and end stacks. 2 storeys and attic; 3-window range. 4-panel door to right of centre with panelled reveals in moulded wood frame with straight hood. Two 3-light casement windows to left. 2-light casements to first floor either side of blocked central window. Long, lower, 2-storey, 3-window secondary range to right with 2-and 3-light casement windows and C20 windows to first floor. All windows have timber lintels. Stonework of secondary range shows signs of disturbance, including one blocked door. Interior not inspected.

Listing NGR: SP5764254695

records.name: WEST ORCHARD FARMHOUSE
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES OLD FORGE LANE SP5754 (North side) 15/115 West Orchard Farmhouse - II Farmhouse. Dated 1754 with earlier origins and C19 additions. Coursed squared ironstone, slate roof, brick end stacks. L-plan. 2 storeys and attic; 4-window range. Left half of finer masonry (straight joint slightly to right of centre) has plank door with overlight, in C19 open timber porch with gabled tile roof and bargeboards, flanked by 2-light casement windows with timber lintels to ground and first floors. Small 1-light leaded window to right of centre and other 2-light casement windows, all with timber lintels. Single-storey brick extension to far right. Plinth and quoins. By garden door to rear datestone inscribed RS 1754. Large C19 wing also to rear. Interior not inspected.

Listing NGR: SP5723954673

records.name: BANK COTTAGE
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES OLD FORGE LANE SP5754 (South side) 15/117 Bank Cottage - II Cottage. Thought to have been formerly row of 3. C17/early C18. Cruck-fraaed. Coursed ironstone rubble, corrugated asbestos roof, ridge stacks. 3-unit plan. 2 storeys; 3-window range. C20 5-panel door left of centre with timber lintel, irregular fenestration to ground floor of one-and two-light casement windows, those to right with concrete lintels. 2-light first floor windows with timber lintels, except for middle window - concrete. Some courses of brick below eaves. Quoins. Interior has riddle cruck truss, probably a full cruck, 3 open fireplaces with timber bressumers, crudely finished spine beans. Formerly thatched.

Listing NGR: SP5745454744

records.name: CHURCH OF ST PETER AND ST PAUL, CHEST TOMB APPROXIMATELY 4 METRES NORTH OF NORTH DOOR
records.officialName: Church of St Peter and St Paul, Chest Tomb Approximately 4 Metres North of North Door
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/104 Church of St. Peter and St. Paul, chest tomb approx. 4m. N of N door GV II Chest tomb. Mid C18. Dressed ironstone and limestone. Stepped plinth, limestone balustered corners, inscriptions on long side commemorating various members of the Shepherd family, 1763-1800.

Listing NGR: SP5742254908

records.name: SWAN FARMHOUSE
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES HIGH STREET SP5754 (East side) 15/113 Swan Farmhouse - II Farmhouse, formerly The Swan Public House. Late C18. Red brick, tile roofs, brick end stacks. Double-depth plan. 2 storeys and attic; 3-window range. Round-arched doorway with C20 door to left of canted bay window on dressed stone base with tripartite sash window to front (12-pane sash to middle section, 4-pane sashes to sides) and 8-pane sashes either side and tile roof. Wood mullion and transom windows to first floor either side of blocked window. Plinth and storey band. A lean-to extension to left side, gable ends to right side painted with two blocked windows with segmental heads to ground floor of back range, 2 12-pane sashes to first floor, both gables with circular attic windows below end stacks. Interior has stop-chamfered spine beams.

Listing NGR: SP5762454532

records.name: CHURCH OF ST PETER AND ST PAUL, STUMP OF CHURCHYARD CROSS APPROXIMATELY 6 METRES SOUTH OF SOUTH AISLE
records.officialName: Church of St Peter and St Paul, Stump of Churchyard Cross Approximately 6 Metres South of South Aisle
records.details:
PRESTON CAPES SP5754 15/103 Church of St. Peter and St. Paul, stump of churchyard cross approx. 6m. S of S aisle GV II Churchyard cross. Medieval. Ironstone. Base and lower portion of octagonal shaft.

Listing NGR: SP5743254881
